Cold-adapted plant lineages distributed across both hemispheres may assemble their ranges either through repeated evolution of cold tolerance or through long-distance dispersal into climates resembling their ancestral niche. We tested these alternatives in the grass genus  Deschampsia  (Poaceae: Pooideae), whose distribution extends from the Holarctic to maritime Antarctica.

The study used an Angiosperms353 target-capture dataset comprising 115 accessions. Of these, 90 accessions represent 34 species of the  Deschampsia  complex, approximately 70% of its described diversity, with herbarium vouchers collected over 157 years (1868–2025) treated as primary genomic material.
